summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: @ecg-internal/aurora-js-formatters 2.0.1 is a stub package whose only functional code is an install- and import-time beacon. The postinstall lifecycle script runs `node beacon.cjs`, which POSTs the package name, `os.hostname()`, `__dirname` (install path), `process.cwd()`, and the Node version to the hardcoded bare-IP HTTP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The declared main `index.js` also calls `require('./beacon.cjs').fire()` at top level and exports a Proxy that returns no-op functions for every property, so the consumer's build keeps running after the beacon fires and does not surface an error. The `@ecg-internal/` scope shape and author comments describing the callback as 'proof of install' are consistent with a dependency-confusion probe targeting an internal package name on the public registry; installing or resolving this name as a transitive dependency leaks internal build-host identifiers to an attacker-controlled address.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
